section.title: System context
section.para: JetOS runs on a module, which it shares between partitions as the configuration says. The partitions are the applications; the ARINC 653 application executive interface that they use, and the C library, are in the library of the partitions, which asks the kernel for its services through system calls. The configuration of the module is made when JetOS is built, and the kernel, the configuration and the images of the partitions are one kernel image, which a boot loader or the firmware starts.

listitem.para: The core of the kernel (kernel/core) schedules the partitions and their processes, keeps the time, loads the partitions, carries messages between ports, handles errors and answers system calls. It does not depend on a processor or a board.

The CPU support packages (kernel/csps) give the core the memory spaces, the contexts of processes, the entry to the kernel from system calls, interrupts and exceptions, and the access to the memory of a partition, for x86_64 and for arm64.
The board support packages (kernel/bsps) give the core the consoles, the interrupt controller, the timer, the clocks and the reset of a board.
The debugging support (kernel/debug), which is present when it is configured, holds the GDB server and the monitor.
The library that the kernel shares with the hypervisor (common/) holds the memory routines and the formatter of the output.
